entry.title: Wits professor urges South Africa to build its own AI capacity, not just import it
entry.summary:
For interview wey im give SAnews for San Jose, as AI delegation wey President Cyril Ramaphosa dey lead go visit Silicon Valley, Wits computer science professor, Benjamin Rosman, wey dey lead di advisory panel wey dey review South Africa national AI policy, talk say South Africa must build dia own AI power, no be to depend on wetin dey happen for oda places. Im point to di universities, researchers and entrepreneurs wey di kontri already have as foundation, im warn say decisions wey dem go take for di next two to five years, about risk like job disruption and cybercrime, go shape di kontri for many years wey dey come.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar six, AI wey get responsibility, ethics, equity and policy, and Pillar four, AI and how graduates fit get job, Rosman im call for make South Africa build dia own AI power, wey dey based on wetin dia universities already know, match wetin Wits AHEAD dey work for: to strengthen Global South power instead of just dey import AI tools wey dem design for oda places.

SAnews (South African Government News Agency) · Government news agency report

entry.title: Universitat Jaume I video: UCL researcher Melissa Bond on AI in higher education teaching and research
entry.summary:
For one video wey Universitat Jaume I, one university for Spain, release, Melissa Bond from University College London talk how generative AI and big language models dey change the way classroom teaching and research dey happen for higher education. Dem record the video for EDUTEC 2026 international conference wey hold for Castelló, and the interview talk about how dem dey use AI well-well for evidence synthesis, dem follow RAISE principles, and how AI tools fit make systematic reviews faster, so researchers fit get more time to shape policy.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar one, generative AI for higher education, and Pillar five, analytics and data for education systems, Bond im call for people to use AI well, make evidence lead di way, na di same thing Wits AHEAD dey talk say AI tools for teaching and research must come with safeguard, no be just excitement.

Universitat Jaume I (EDUTEC 2026 international conference) · University conference video

entry.title: US study builds a behavioural early warning system from ordinary online course clicks
entry.summary:
One study wey dem publish for Issues in Information Systems, wey researchers from Georgia College and State University for America do, build one early warning system wey dey based on how students dey behave, from 32,593 students and more than 10.6 million click wey dem make for Open University Learning Analytics Dataset. Dem use four measurement wey show how students dey consistent, how dem dey intense, and how dem dey space dia study time, and one logistic regression model fit correctly show students wey go fail 81 percent of di time, e reach overall accuracy of 62.6 percent afta only 30 days of data and 68.7 percent by day 150. Study time wey dem space well-well and regular dey connect to success, while study time wey too intense dey connect to higher risk to fail.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar two, AI and prediction analytics for student success, retention and early warning, dis behavioural early warning model, wey dem build from ordinary click wey learning system already dey record instead of new expensive tools, dey give Wits AHEAD one practical template to spot students wey dey risk early enough for big online and mixed courses for Global South.

Issues in Information Systems, Georgia College and State University · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Office for Students and Advance HE report says AI detection cannot be trusted to protect degree standards
entry.summary:
For 11 November 2026, Office for Students and Advance HE release one report wey dem call Making AI Work for Students, wey dem base on more than 300 students and staff from more than 120 England higher education institutions, wey dem survey between June to September 2026. Di report find out say unsupervised assessment fit often complete well with generative AI, say detection tools no fit reliably catch AI use, and say most institutions' approach just come from individual staff dey try things, no be from top leadership strategy. Training for AI literacy for students and staff still dey uneven and mostly na optional.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar one, generative AI for higher education: teaching, assessment and integrity, na system-wide evidence be dis, no be just one university policy, and di warning say detection no fit reliable, e strengthen di point wey Wits AHEAD don dey make for long time, say make dem redesign assessment instead of just dey police am.

Office for Students and Advance HE · National regulator and sector body joint report

entry.title: Randomised trial finds course integrated AI tutor lowered grades and cut engagement for US undergraduates
entry.summary:
One randomised trial wey get 2,379 undergraduate students and 30 lecturers for one big public university for United States show say access to AI tutor wey dem build inside course reduce final grades by 0.37 standard deviation, and e reduce how students dey use di learning platform by 0.90 standard deviation, compare to sections wey no get di tutor. Di researchers, wey Jing Liu and Tracy Sweet lead, report say di loss pass well-well for first generation students, dem conclude say di tutor just replace di study work wey dey there already, e no improve learning.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar one, generative AI for higher education, and pillar two, AI and predictive analytics for student success, dis finding say AI tutor wey no get guide fit widen gap for first generation students na warning wey Wits AHEAD dey take serious as dem dey design AI support for Global South students wey get dia own access and preparation gap.

IZA Institute of Labor Economics working paper by Jing Liu, Tracy Sweet and colleagues · Working paper, randomised controlled trial

entry.title: Google.org-funded AI Research Foundations programme begins training South African university lecturers
entry.summary:
Di AI Research Foundations programme, wey Google.org dey fund, start for South Africa on 9 November 2026 wit five-day workshop for university lecturers for Stellenbosch University Biomedical Research Institute, wey bring together academics from Stellenbosch, University of Venda, University of Mpumalanga, University of Free State and University of Western Cape. Na FATE Foundation and African Institute for Mathematical Sciences South Africa dey run am, wit curriculum wey Google DeepMind build wit University College London, dis train-di-trainer programme wan reach ten South African universities as part of bigger target of thirty universities across Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria and South Africa, wey go train 30,000 students for total.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar four, AI, graduate capability, employability and just transitions, dis train-di-trainer model wey give lecturers power pass students only, dey matter for how fast South African universities fit build AI research capacity wey go last, instead of to dey depend on one-off workshop.

Innovation Village (AI Africa Intelligence digest), reporting the Google.org-funded AI Research Foundations launch · Technology news digest report on a philanthropically funded university training programme

entry.title: Guiding students to use an AI tutor well matters more than just giving them access, Chilean field experiment finds
entry.summary:
One randomised field experiment for undergraduate economics course for one Chilean university, wey dem report inside IZA Institute of Labor Economics working paper wey Sebastian Gallegos of Universidad Adolfo Ibáñez write, test one course specific AI study assistant for seven sections. Just to encourage students to adopt di tool before midterm raise awareness and use, but e no change midterm score, while to guide students to use am like tutor, as dem dey work through concepts step by step, before final exam raise final exam performance by 0.22 standard deviation and perceived usefulness by 0.38 standard deviation, mostly for open response questions.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar one, generative AI for higher education, dis finding, say how dem guide student to use AI assistant matter pass just to give dem access, dey talk directly to how Wits AHEAD dey design AI supported teaching across Global South.

IZA Institute of Labor Economics working paper by Sebastian Gallegos (Universidad Adolfo Ibanez) · Working paper, randomised field experiment

entry.title: Universities clone lecturers as AI avatars to extend teaching support

category.term: United Kingdom, United States and Australia

entry.summary:
Imperial Business School, Harvard Business School, Columbia University School of Nursing and Gies College of Business for University of Illinois dey among di schools wey dey build AI avatar of dia lecturers to extend teaching support pass classroom. Imperial start to clone lecturers since 2024, starting with Professor David Shrier, so dat students wey dey far or overseas fit reach digital version of dia lecturer any time; Gies College of Business now don get like twelve lecturers wey get voice or video clone, wey dem dey update by edit script instead of record di whole class again. One pilot for University of Northampton find out say students like di access but dem worry say dem fit lose personal connection, so di pilot recommend guardrails wey fit adjust, wey go send sensitive question to human staff.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD first pillar, generative AI for higher education, dis one show how di technology dey move from simple chatbot to lecturer avatar wey carry dia own voice; di guardrails wey dis universities dey already build, including to send sensitive question to human being, dey show lesson for any school wey wan try di same thing.

Times Higher Education · Established press

entry.title: AI-detection tools keep flagging non-native English writers as cheats, researchers warn

category.term: Global, with examples from South Africa and the Philippines

entry.summary:
For one piece wey e write for University World News, health informatics scholar Davis Austria warn say di AI-detection tools wey many universities dey rely on, dey often mark English wey non-native speakers write as if AI write am, e quote research about writers from South Africa and Philippines wey dia sentence style dey mistake for machine work. One 2026 study wey test detectors for master's thesis wey non-native English speakers write find out say Turnitin no fit correctly mark even one of di papers wey AI write fully, while Pangram perform best; one earlier study find say just to add spelling mistake fit reduce one detector accuracy from 39.5% to 12.9%. For one case wey England and Wales Office of di Independent Adjudicator review, one student explain say e use Google to find similar words, because English no be im native language, but dem take dat one as confession say e use AI, wey cause mark reduction for im whole degree, one decision wey di ombudsman later see say no evidence support am.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD sixth pillar, fairness for AI wey dey responsible, dis one dey big warning say detection tools wey dem train mainly with native English fit punish Global South own students pass anybody, and say detector score suppose start conversation with student instead of stand alone as proof.

University World News · Established press (commentary citing peer-reviewed research)

entry.title: East African Community adopts a regional AI strategy with universities at its centre

category.term: East Africa (Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, South Sudan)

entry.summary:
Di education ministers for East African Community (EAC) don agree one regional plan for artificial intelligence (AI) for di 21st Sectoral Council meeting wey happun for Kampala, from 27 to 31 October 2026, dem approve one basic AI course for undergraduate students for any field, plus one Regional AI Network of Universities wey go coordinate AI teaching, research and new ideas across di region. Di Inter-University Council for East Africa go now make one plan to run di course, universities wey dey ready fit try di course first, and three new papers go guide teacher training, school policy and how people suppose behave. For di new Ayre AI readiness index wey Commonwealth release, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania and Rwanda all score below di benchmark, but Kenya dey top with 48.7 out of 100.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD fifth pillar, wey be analytics and data for education systems, dis one na one of di first regional group wey turn AI plan to real university curriculum rule and one network wey everybody share, instead of make every school dey do dia own thing alone.

TechTrendsKE · Intergovernmental body (reported by specialist technology press)

entry.title: Google DeepMind and Fab AI to build open AI tools for African teachers
entry.summary:
Google DeepMind and di non-profit Fab AI, wey Google.org and Gates Foundation dey fund together, go work with local innovators for Kenya, Ghana and South Africa to build teacher tools wey dey use open Gemma models, for lesson planning, feedback and coaching, wey go work for cheap device and dey fit local language and curriculum. Di first phase wan reach up to 500 teachers and 15,000 pupils, and dem go share di data, test tools and models open so make other people fit use am too. One free Google AI Educator Series dey also expand for di region, dem go start for South Africa with South African Council for Educators before dem reach Nigeria, Kenya and Ghana for 2027.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar three, AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, open model wey dem build for local language and curriculum matter well well for scale across Global South, pass any single tool wey need license.

Google (Africa blog) · Official company and non-profit announcement

entry.title: Universities push AI firms to be more transparent on costs
entry.summary:
Jisc, di UK sector body, wey Universities UK and Guild HE support, don release one call to suppliers wey ask AI companies to agree common terms for price, usage data and governance before universities go sign any contract. Dia six expectations include warning make price no just dey rise anyhow, make dem still fit use certain model version when teaching or research need di same result again, and protection from change wey go disturb work or make school dey depend on one supplier only. Jisc licensing director, Caren Milloy, talk say universities need to sure say dem still dey control dia cost, choice and risk as more people dey use AI.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar six, responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, dis one na one rare case where universities come together to set terms for AI suppliers, instead of make each one dey negotiate alone.

Times Higher Education · Established higher education trade press

entry.title: Case study of a Portuguese data science school finds generative AI entering teaching cautiously and unevenly
entry.summary:
New case study wey dem publish for Frontiers in Education on 13 November 2026 show say generative AI dey enter teaching for one Portugal data science school small small, as trial and no evenly. Dem interview eight lecturers and dem find out say six of dem don already sabi generative AI, mostly from teaching demsef, na only four get any training from di school, and seven don change how dem dey teach, mostly dem dey use AI as helper for writing, brainstorming and coding. To protect assessment, five lecturers add critical-thinking questions, four change go oral exam or project defence, and three bring back short face-to-face test wey no get network access.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Wits AHEAD first pillar na generative AI for higher education, wey cover teaching, assessment and integrity; di study call for clear institution policy, time and money for staff training, and fair access for students to AI tools, na di same gap wey Wits AHEAD dey work to close for Southern Africa universities.

Frontiers in Education (Pereira and Aparicio, NOVA Information Management School, Universidade NOVA de Lisboa) · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Universities across Asia-Pacific pair data science students with community organisations to close a data gap

category.term: Philippines, Hong Kong, Singapore and Japan

entry.summary:
One forum wey happen for Manila on 7 November 2026, wey University World News report, show how Association of Pacific Rim Universities (APRU) and di non-profit data.org match university data science teams with community organisations across Asia-Pacific. Students for Chinese University of Hong Kong change sustainability reports of almost 1,900 members, wey bin dey lock inside text-heavy PDF, to dashboard for Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil, while one University of the Philippines team build database and field app wey fit work without network, wey around 125 farming and fishing communities dey use now. Di event mark di end of two-year pilot, di Social Impact Data Science Accelerator, wey Mastercard Center for Inclusive Growth support.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Wits AHEAD fifth pillar na analytics and data for education systems and decision-making; di accelerator show one model wey fit transfer, wey match university data science training with real organisation data, wey Wits AHEAD fit learn from as dem dey build similar capacity for Southern Africa.

University World News (Kalinga Seneviratne) · Established higher education press

entry.title: South African ICT skills survey finds AI skills demand outpacing university and TVET pipelines
entry.summary:
Di 2026 IITPSA ICT Skills Survey, wey Institute of Information Technology Professionals South Africa run togeda wit Africa Analysis, wey dem release on 30 October 2026, show say demand for AI skills, AI engineers, machine learning engineers, generative AI specialists, prompt engineers and AI governance officers, dey rise pass wetin South Africa university and TVET fit supply. Around 80 percent of ICT practitioners wey dem ask talk say AI done already reduce dia workload or make task simple, as di survey blame di skills shortage on lack of workplace experience, education and training gap, low diversity and brain drain of experienced professionals.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Wits AHEAD fourth pillar na AI, graduate capability and employability. Di survey call for workplace-based learning and stronger industry-university partnership dey show di gap between wetin university dey teach and wetin South Africa AI economy need now.

ITWeb (IITPSA and Africa Analysis) · Industry workforce survey (IITPSA and Africa Analysis)

entry.title: Study of five African countries finds AI adoption in universities outpacing curriculum and policy change

category.term: Ghana, Rwanda, Namibia, Kenya and Zambia

entry.summary:
One study by Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology RetAIn project, wey dem publish for Frontiers in Education and Ghana News Agency report on 23 October 2026, survey 156 people and hold focus group wit 77 stakeholders across Ghana, Rwanda, Namibia, Kenya and Zambia. Di study show say universities don adopt AI tools pass how dem change curriculum, lecturer training or governance, and say around half of di respondents name cost, like school fees, data and device, as big wahala, as women, students wit disability, and rural, low-income and part-time students fit suffer pass to dey left behind.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Wits AHEAD sixth pillar na responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy. Di study kain findings for each country, policy wey no dey implement for Rwanda, curriculum wey dey lag for Namibia, initiative wey no coordinate for Ghana, dey show di governance gap wey Wits AHEAD dey watch across Global South.

Ghana News Agency, reporting a Frontiers in Education study by KNUST's RetAIn project · National news agency report on a peer-reviewed study

entry.title: Office for Students tells universities to bring back in-person exams to protect assessment from AI
entry.summary:
Office for Students, di body wey dey oversee universities for England, don tell universities say dem need to think about going back to face to face exams wey no gree open book, viva voce and practical tasks, so dat assessment go still dey valid as AI dey spread well well. Di guidance come after one four month study wey dem do wit Advance HE, wey base on tori wit around 300 students and staff for more than 120 schools, and e show say AI use dey everywhere, and say some assessments no fit work well again. Na di first time di regulator don lay out di kain AI wahala for school wey fit make dem take action, including say school fit get lower quality award.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Wits AHEAD first pillar na generative AI for higher education, including assessment and integrity. Na im make wen one national regulator move from just guidance to action wey fit bite, e dey show sign wey oda systems, including South Africa own, go dey watch well well.

Times Higher Education · Established higher education press

entry.title: Graduates' wellbeing and civic contribution should be tracked alongside pay, British Academy argues
entry.summary:
British Academy talk say di way dem dey measure wetin make graduate successful too narrow, because e dey focus only on salary. Di Academy want dem begin track work life balance, long term health and civic engagement too. Dem point to one government survey wey show say 24% of graduates dey volunteer well well at least once every month, compare to 17% for people wey no graduate, and dem suggest say make dem link higher education data wit health and crime data so dem fit see fuller picture.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Wits AHEAD fourth pillar na about graduate capability and work wey dem fit do pass di first job. Wen one national academy dey push make dem measure outcome wider, e dey tally wit how di group dey define "success" for dia own candidates.

British Academy, reported by Times Higher Education · National academy report

entry.title: South Africa ranks second in Africa on new Commonwealth youth AI readiness index, behind Mauritius
entry.summary:
Di 2026 Commonwealth Youth AI Readiness Index, wey Ayre Think Tank put togeda from 1,128 sources across all 56 Commonwealth countries, put South Africa for number 13 position overall wit 56.8 out of 100, number two for Africa, just behind Mauritius (64.4, number eight for world). Di index project say AI fit add between US$4.7 billion to US$13.7 billion to South Africa economy within ten years, depending on di scenario.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Wits AHEAD sixth pillar na responsible AI, equity and policy. Kain national readiness index like dis one dey shape di policy case for investment for AI skills and governance across Global South.

University World News (from African Insider) · Established higher education press

entry.title: Youth unemployment eases slightly to 47.3% as overall unemployment rises to 33.7% in the third quarter of 2026
entry.summary:
Di official unemployment rate climb by 0.1 percentage point to 33.7% for Q3 2026, as employment grow by 101,000 to 16.8 million, but di workforce grow pass dat. Youth unemployment (15 to 34) drop small by 0.1 percentage point to 47.3%: unemployed youth drop by 23,000 to 5.0 million, while employed youth drop by 5,000 to 5.5 million.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis na di number di group dey use for graduate pathways and just transitions. Pillar 4 dey ask whether AI dey close or open dis gap for dis same group of people.

Statistics South Africa · National statistics office

entry.title: University AI policies focus on cheating but leave data risks largely unaddressed, commentary warns
entry.summary:
One commentary for University World News talk say universities don write detailed rules against AI-assisted cheating, but dem leave small guidance on how staff and researchers fit put institution, student or research data inside AI tools. E quote one UK survey wey show say 63% of 49 higher education institutions don already adopt some AI tool, but na 37% only check risk pass dia immediate supplier, e also talk about data leak for University of Osaka wey affect 77,851 people, as reminder say di bigger risk na usually ordinary data mistake, no be di AI model itself.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 6, wey be responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, dis one dey remind us to check say AI governance for universities, including dis group own, dey cover data handling, no be academic integrity only.

University World News · Established higher education press (commentary)

entry.title: Wits opens a Global Higher Education Futures Centre, with a dedicated generative AI pedagogy hub
entry.summary:
University of Witwatersrand (Wits) don officially open dia Global Higher Education Futures Centre, wey dem launch for one webinar on 30 September wey over 170 teachers, institution leaders and policymakers attend. Di centre dey built around nine hubs, including one wey dey focus on generative AI teaching methods, and dem design am as answer to wetin di founders call polycrisis, na climate breakdown, geopolitical tension, generative AI disruption and inequality for Global South. Di founder, Professor Ruksana Osman, and di director, Dr Bernadette Johnson, tok say di centre go put Global South knowledge for front, instead of import ready-made models from north.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 6, one South African university dey build dia own framework to think about how AI dey disrupt higher education, instead of use one wey dem build somewhere else, and dis na exactly di Global South-led, equity-centred approach wey Wits AHEAD dey support.

University of the Witwatersrand · University announcement

entry.title: Wording of university generative AI policies shapes how students and teachers actually behave, study finds
entry.summary:
Some researchers check di generative AI policies from 101 universities for United States, dem also tok to 20 students and 20 lecturers to sabi how di rules dey work for real life. Dem find out say di exact wording of a rule, no be just wetin di rule talk, fit change how students behave: rule wey dem build around dishonesty make students hide dia AI use because of fear, while rule wey dem build around accountability encourage dem to dey open about am. Di lecturers sef tok say dem get extra approval work for hand, and dem no get reliable way to check if students dey comply.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 1, dis study remind us say generative AI policy no fit better pass how dem word am: universities wey dey write or change dia own rules on AI for teaching and assessment need to test no be only wetin di rule allow, but how students and staff go read and act on di words demsef.

arXiv preprint (University of Maryland and University of Iowa researchers) · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: How deeply students engage with an AI chat, not how often they use it, predicts better coursework, large Australian study finds
entry.summary:
Researchers for University of Queensland and Monash University study 1,681 students across 40 university courses wey dey use AI companion wey dem build inside resource creation, peer moderation and practice work. Dem code 829 conversation threads to check cognitive engagement, dem also model almost 3,000 task sequences, dem find out say students wey engage AI well-well, no be just students wey dey chat with am plenty-plenty, na dem produce better final work, no matter how many message dem exchange. After one wrong attempt, students wey talk to AI try less, but dem dey correct well-well when dem try again.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 2, dis finding important for any institution wey dey build analytics around AI tool use: to just count how many time students open chatbot no tell you anything serious about learning, so systems wey suppose support student success need to check how deep di engagement be, no be how many time dem click.

University of Queensland and Monash University (arXiv preprint, submitted to the Journal of Computer Assisted Learning) · Working paper (arXiv preprint, submitted to the Journal of Computer Assisted Learning)

entry.title: Grade the process, not just the AI-era output, Bristol pro vice-chancellor tells student success conference
entry.summary:
For one Student Success UK and Ireland conference wey Times Higher Education organise, Tansy Jessop, wey be pro vice-chancellor for education and students for University of Bristol, tok say universities don pass di stage wia dem just dey police how students use generative AI well-well, dem need to design assessment wey go show how student reach im answer instead. She explain one computer science case for Bristol, where robot-design work dem submit na pure AI-generated most times, and dis make staff to just give students one complete robot, make dem find out how dem build am. Jessop tok say dis approach go help students develop skills wey AI no fit easily replace, like curiosity, critical thinking and collaboration.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 1, dis one give real, classroom-level answer to di assessment integrity question: instead of dey chase unreliable AI detectors, make dem build tasks wey go show how student dey think, and make human still dey di one wey judge.

Times Higher Education · Established higher education press

entry.title: AI-generated 'slop' papers published under prominent academics' names without their consent
entry.summary:
Some journals wey resemble each other dey publish papers wey AI generate, dem put am for name of popular academics, including Jure Leskovec and Fei-Fei Li from Stanford, wey talk say dem never write or submit di work at all. Times Higher Education report say one paper come back again under different author name few days after dem flag am and remove am, and di journals dey share di same editor-in-chief and board members wey no even know say dem dey list dem. Di three journals, wey dem register for 2026 only, dey charge authors between ten and two hundred US dollars for each paper.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 6, dis one show how generative AI fit use create not just research findings, but researchers' own identity too, na why responsible AI policy for higher education must reach publishing integrity, no be only classroom.

Times Higher Education · Established higher education press

entry.title: Staff overestimate how much students use generative AI, Manchester study finds
entry.summary:
One study wey dem do for one social science school for one university for United Kingdom show say university staff dey over-estimate how often students dey use generative AI for their study. Based on questions wey dem ask 45 staff and 86 students for University of Manchester, staff rate students' AI use as 5.23 for scale of seven, well pass students own average wey be 3.11. Students too show say dem happy pass staff about how AI fit help productivity and learning, dem talk say dem dey use am mostly to find answer, write work and fix grammar.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 1, di gap between wetin staff think and wetin students really dey do show why policy on generative AI and how dem dey design teaching need to stand on evidence wey come from students demsef, no be staff own assumption, as universities for Global South too dey think about similar assumption.

Frontiers in Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Habit, not enjoyment, drives ChatGPT use among distance students at the University of South Africa, study of 294 finds
entry.summary:
One study of 294 students for University of South Africa, di biggest distance education institution for Africa, use di UTAUT2 model check why students dey use ChatGPT. Habit na di strongest thing wey predict both di plan to use ChatGPT and di real use, then facilitating conditions like guidance and resources follow, but enjoyment and wetin friends think no make any serious difference. Di model explain 69.2% of di students' plan to use di tool and 37.9% of how dem really use am.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 1, di finding say habit and support from di institution, no be say di thing new, na im dey drive use, show say universities suppose shape how students dey use AI every day through guidance and course design, especially for distance learning for di Global South.

Frontiers in Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Africa and Europe seek their own path on AI in science, with shared computing and genomic data on the agenda
entry.summary:
For one African Union and European Union meeting on AI for science on 26 October, wey dem do online instead of for Addis Ababa as dem plan, European Commission official Maria Cristina Russo talk say United States and China don move very far ahead and say Europe and Africa need dia own way. Speakers call for shared regional computing, one continent-wide framework for genomic data and benefit sharing, and targets wey dem fit measure for women, wey be about one-fifth of di world data and AI workforce. Di recommendations go reach AU-EU research and innovation ministers meeting wey dem shift go 2027, University World News report.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 6, dis meeting put data ownership, fair access to computing power and movement of talent for di centre of AI policy, questions wey go decide weda African universities go shape AI for research or dem go just dey use am.

University World News · Established higher education press

entry.title: UNESCO: university enrolment in the Arab States has nearly tripled to almost 15 million, yet youth unemployment stands at 26%
entry.summary:
New UNESCO report, The state of higher education in the Arab States, find say di number of university students for di region don almost triple inside 25 years, reach almost 15 million students, but di enrolment rate, wey be 37% for 2024, still dey below di world average of 44%. Women now be almost half of di STEM graduates for di region, compare to just over one-third for di whole world, but youth unemployment don reach 26%, almost double di world average. Dem launch di report for Doha on 4 November, e get ten recommendations, and e note say more than 70% of Arab States don put digital goals inside dia national higher education plan.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 5, dis one show wetin regional higher education data fit reveal: plenty access no mean much if di system no dey check weda graduates dey find work, di same test wey South Africa and di whole Global South dey face.

UNESCO (IESALC and UNESCO Office Beirut) · Intergovernmental body report

entry.title: Deep Learning Indaba video: Vukosi Marivate on governing AI in Africa and what a degree is worth now
entry.summary:
For one 36-minute interview wey dem record during Deep Learning Indaba 2026 for Pan-Atlantic University for Lagos, Professor Vukosi Marivate, wey co-found di Indaba, Masakhane NLP and Lelapa AI, and one of di 40 experts for di United Nations Independent International Scientific Panel on AI, explain wetin e mean to advise government on AI and why to govern AI for South Africa touch every ministry. E talk say sovereignty mean power to take action, no be to build everything for house, say AI no break assessment but e expose am, and say Africa suppose move from brain drain go brain circulation.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 4, im questions about wetin degree worth for dis AI time, and weda Africa dey train cheap AI labour for export, touch di heart of graduate capability and just transitions for di Global South.

Deep Learning Indaba (YouTube) · Africa's machine learning community, official video channel

entry.title: South Korea vows to prosecute students using AI glasses in exams
entry.summary:
South Korea Ministry of Education talk say from next year, dem go treat cheating for national university entrance exam wit AI smart glasses as criminal matter, after dem catch three students wey wear di device during essay exam for Seoul universities. From 2027, anybody dem catch go face three-year ban from di exam, instead of one year now, and inspectors go dey all di 1,312 exam centre to watch suspicious glasses.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Na clear sign of how fast generative AI tools dey overtake exam integrity rule worldwide (Pillar 1), and reminder say detection and punishment na only part of di answer wey universities and system go need.

Times Higher Education · Established press

entry.title: AI Article Reviews Dominate Human Peer Reviews at Their Best: Evidence and Policy Choices
entry.summary:
Gary King and Steven Worthington wey dey Harvard Institute for Quantitative Social Science compare peer review wey AI write wit 134 human review for 124 manuscript wey dem collect between 2019 and 2026. Dem report say di review wey Claude Opus 4.8 generate pass di human review for every measure wey dem build, dem judge am to be more accurate for dia own check, and three former journal editor prefer am for most of di head-to-head comparison.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Na serious, data-based challenge for how dem dey use generative AI for academic work, no be only for classroom (Pillar 1): if AI fit review research well, universities and journals need policy for when and how to use am, no be just whether to ban am.

Institute for Quantitative Social Science, Harvard University · University working paper

entry.title: Proposal 14: Student outcomes indicators
entry.summary:
England higher education regulator, Office for Students, don propose to change di one single pass-or-fail level wey dem dey use measure graduate progression to three measures wey dem go compare for dia Teaching Excellence Framework: continuing progression to work or more school, how graduates salary compare to national benchmark, and whether graduates talk say dem dey use wetin dem learn, based on Graduate Outcomes survey. Dem go adjust dis measures based on course, location, entry qualification, and students socio-economic background, instead of dey use one fixed national level for all course.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Na real test for Pillar 5 main question: whether data system wey dem build from plenty benchmark measures, instead of one hard national level, fit judge higher education outcomes well well and improve dem.

Office for Students (OfS) · National regulator consultation

entry.title: UCT engineering pairs AI-enabled early warning with a multilingual support hub to lift student success
entry.summary:
Researchers for University of Cape Town Faculty of Engineering and the Built Environment dey describe a Student Success Project wey combine early risk-assessment framework, mentorship wey senior students dey lead, and one data-driven, AI-enabled support hub. Dis hub come wit multilingual digital glossary for isiXhosa, Sesotho, Kiswahili and Afrikaans, wey dey address language marginalisation alongside academic risk. Di chapter dey appear inside Constellations of Hope, one Club of Rome report on transformative learning.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Na correct, verified South African example of predictive analytics for student success (pillar two) wey dem build around multilingual fairness, e dey show say early warning data go only help students if di support wey follow am still dey speak dia language.

Globethics Publications (Club of Rome report) · Peer-reviewed book chapter

entry.title: AI literacy alone does not create graduate opportunity, Nigerian study of 450 students finds; technology readiness is what matters
entry.summary:
One survey of 450 Nigerian university students show say both entrepreneurship education and AI literacy dey raise students' technology readiness, and say na dis readiness sabi predict whether dem go turn AI tools into real micro-entrepreneurial business. Wen students feel say resource dey scarce, e dey weaken dia entrepreneurial action directly, but e dey strengthen di link between readiness and action once students don get di tools.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Na direct evidence for pillar four: access to AI alone no fit create opportunity for graduates wey dey tight-resource settings; na capability-building and technology readiness dey turn AI literacy into real human capability and livelihood.

Journal of Entrepreneurship in Emerging Economies · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Computational text indicators fail to improve, and can worsen, predictions of academic results, Salvadoran study warns
entry.summary:
Researchers for Universidad Salvadoreña Alberto Masferrer test whether machine-learning text indicators of students' epistemic norms fit improve prediction of academic results pass simple household and resource data. Among 263 students wey dem observe for two waves for five sites, di computer indicators no add any reliable predictive value, and one version even make prediction significantly worse after dem correct for multiple comparisons.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Na clear warning for pillar five: AI-derived text or behaviour proxy no suppose dey treated as fit for high-stakes education decisions without strong testing, na discipline wey Wits AHEAD dey apply for dia own analytics work.

Journal of Applied Research in Higher Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: LMS activity, pacing and attendance are the strongest predictors of retention in blended courses, Turkish study finds
entry.summary:
One study for Journal of Higher Education Policy and Management, wey İrfan Ayhan of Kırşehir Ahi Evran University for Türkiye write, check how predictive analytics wey dem take from learning-management-system activity, pace, assessment behaviour and attendance fit show students wey dey for risk for blended higher education courses. E find out say dis signs na di strongest tins wey fit predict retention, and e argue say, if dem use am well, predictive analytics fit strengthen early-warning systems and guide institution strategy, as far as institutions dey also think about di ethics of how dem dey use dat kain data.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD work wey dey about AI and predictive analytics for student success, dis study remind us say di data wey already dey sidon for most universities' learning-management systems, no be only new AI tools, fit power one early-warning system wey dey work well if dem combine am with clear ethical framework.

Journal of Higher Education Policy and Management · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Short hands-on workshop lifts science teachers' confidence in using AI for adaptive teaching, German pilot study finds
entry.summary:
One pilot study wey dem publish for Frontiers in Education, wey Mathea Brückner, Christoph Thyssen and Johannes Huwer, from di universities of Konstanz, Pädagogische Hochschule Thurgau and Pädagogische Hochschule Freiburg do, test whether one short, hands-on workshop fit raise lower-secondary science teachers' confidence for how dem dey use AI do adaptive teaching. For one before-and-after study wey involve 16 multiplier teachers for Germany, both teachers' feeling say AI dey useful and dia own confidence wey dem report demsef, rise well-well after di workshop, and di two tins only come dey strongly connect after dat time. Di authors warn say dis small sample, wey dem self report, show change, but e no prove say di workshop na im cause lasting improvement.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar wey dey about AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, dis study show one practical, cheap format, short hands-on workshop, wey teacher-training programmes fit test and adapt to build science teachers' confidence for AI tools.

Frontiers in Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: World Bank video: 'small AI', not big models alone, can widen opportunity in developing-economy education and jobs
entry.summary:
For di Global AI and Digital Summit wey happen for Seoul, wey World Bank Group record, dia President, Ajay Banga, open one panel discussion about how "small AI", wey be practical tools wey fit local condition, no be only big general model, fit increase opportunity for developing economy. Nigeria Minister of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, Bosun Tijani, join Tridge CEO Hoshik Shin and Amini founder Kate Kallot discuss education, farming and public service, including one part wey talk about lesson wey dem learn from how dem dey use AI for education for El Salvador. Di panel talk say reliable local data, affordable connection, computing power, skill and procurement system na di conditions wey go make local innovators fit scale dia AI solutions.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD work wey dey about AI, graduate capability, employability and just transition, dis discussion show say AI promise dey depend on practical conditions, skill, infrastructure and procurement, wey go decide whether developing economy universities and system go really benefit, no be only dia mate for Global North wey get more resources.

World Bank Group (YouTube) · International financial institution, official video channel
